newsitem.title: GREECE: Ecu up vs drachma, depos soft, bonds, forwards hold.
newsitem.headline: Ecu up vs drachma, depos soft, bonds, forwards hold.

text.p: The ecu continued to gain ground against the drachma in early dealings trading around 310.48/58, depos were easier across-the-board, forex forwards were little changed and bonds were holding with two-year zeros on sale today, dealers said.
Greek markets were closed on May Day.

"The drachma is weaker against the ecu," said a forex dealer at a private bank. "We can see much higher ecu/drachma levels in a very short period of time if the central bank sticks to its current hands-off approach."

The central bank has signalled that it is comfortable with the current high ecu/drachma levels which exceed the end-96 ecu/drachma rate by more than 1.0 percent raising doubts about its hard drachma policy, the trader said.

"The market opened with wider spreads in ecu/drachma and hit 310.60/80 before easing a bit," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "We have seen some ecu buying from abroad in the last few days and especially after Deutsche's report on Wednesday."
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said that volatility in ecu/drachma raised doubts about the central bank's commitment to the hard drachma policy that aims to reduce inflation.
Depos were softer about five basis points from one week to one year periods on excess liquidity and forex forwards were holding, dealers said.
Bond dealers said prices of FRNs and fixed coupon bonds were holding and the market focused on the sale of two-year zeros.
Greece issues two-year zeros at a gross rate of 9.9 percent on Friday.

"I expect the zeros to sell well today, perhaps as much as 400 billion drachmas," said a bond trader at a private bank. "Sooner or later the retail has to shift to two-year zeros from 12-month T-bills."
The mark was quoted at 159.33/43 from Wednesday's 158.425 fix, the dollar at 274.67/77 drachmas from 274.400 and the ecu at 310.51/61 from 309.400 drachmas.
